author: nonretail_writer
central_thesis: Peak-rates relief is the organising idea at the 2023-11-08 cutoff: a Fed hold, a 150,000 payroll print and Treasury auctions absorbed despite larger sizes pulled the 10Y down 30 bps in five observations to 4.58% and VIX to 14.81, lifting long-duration growth while energy funded the rally as WTI fell 10.00% over 20 sessions. We lean into duration and earnings-backed growth (semis, platforms, Polish banks and consumers) but treat the -33 bps inverted curve, rising card delinquencies and WeWork's bankruptcy as evidence that part of the disinflation is a growth scare.
sources_policy: Facts come only from own-date headlines (tools/digest.py 2023-11-08) cited in the same part, or from the 2023-11-08 market card; no later-dated feeds, cards or web material were used. Spot-FX levels are not quoted; currency direction is taken only from cited headlines; DXY is quoted as an index. After-close US reports on 2023-11-07 (Rivian, Lucid, Robinhood, Bumble) are treated as completed results, with the card closes explicitly described as pre-report.
known_ambiguities_omitted: n0059 and n0060 (RBA hike headlines indexed 2023-11-06 08:00 UTC, before the 2023-11-07 decision): misdated index time; same-day 2023-11-07 items n0070, n0071, n0074 used instead.
n0062 ('7 November 2023 | Minutes of the Monetary Policy Meeting'): minutes of the 7 November meeting cannot exist at this cutoff; misdated.
n0907 (Nintendo stocks jump on Zelda movie): the share reaction likely refers to the 2023-11-08 Tokyo session, after cutoff; not used.
n0703 (Taylor Swift named Time's person of the year), n1944, n0112, n1794, n1842, n1916, n0792 (titles referencing 2026): later-dated content under 2023 index dates; not used.
n0755 ('Buffett Cuts Cash') contradicts n0685/n0688 (record cash hoard); the contradictory item was not used.
n1969 (Virginia election live results page): rolling live page, not used.
n1610 (NBP fixing table with a euro rate): numeric spot-FX content, not used.
n1852 (core PCE 'spiked to 3.6%' blog headline): figure ambiguous versus official data; not used.
n1625 (Money.pl 'new sick man of Europe'): country not named in the headline; not used to avoid attributing data to the wrong economy.
No own-date preview dates the RPP/NBP decision or the APEC meeting day; both are described without a calendar date.
